sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Celtchair was an Irish warrior. The Celts treated hospitality as a grave duty. Celtchair broke that rule when blood touched the Fidchell board. King Concobar Mac Nessa sat there playing against the hero Cúchulainn. To clear his good name, Celtchair accepted three hard trials. He completed two of them. Then he slew a dread dog that tormented the land. The beast's poisonous blood spattered him and brought his death. His reputation remained unspoiled.

okr.objective: Celtchair is the Irish hero who repaired his reputation and died with honor.
key_results: He spilled blood on the Fidchell board at a game between king and Cúchulainn.
He completed two of three impossible tasks.
He killed the spectral dog that plagued the land.
The dog's poisonous blood ended his life.
